own_solution.law: At galvanometer null, R_left/R_sample = 41.5/58.5. Thus R_sample = 12(58.5/41.5) = 16.9157 Ω, and resistivity = R_sample πd²/(4L).
assumptions: The uniform bridge wire has resistance proportional to length.
The sample has uniform circular cross section.
The lamp battery circuit is electrically separate from the bridge.
The stated balance position applies after any modification made before balancing.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The resistance-increment variants do not consistently preserve the stipulated number and unit: TE5F9 and TD741 replace 9.4 Ω with an unspecified small amount, while earlier-trial variants also change the temporal condition.

counterexamples: TE5F9 permits a rheostat increment of 0.1 Ω, whereas T0506 specifies 9.4 Ω, so these renderings do not preserve the numerical quantity.
T459C leaves an additional 9.4 Ω in the left arm during balancing and gives 1.42155e-6 Ω m; TAB0A confines that addition to an earlier trial and gives 7.97132e-7 Ω m.
notes: The base problem and each individual rendering are physically solvable. The invalid verdict concerns the stipulated variant construction. Both bridge-diameter sentences give the same 0.65 mm value; the bridge cross-sectional area cancels from its resistance ratio. For T0CEE and T459C the effective left-arm resistance is 21.4 Ω. Resistance used for an earlier trial only is absent during the reported measurement and is classified D.
